research_mode: official Police.uk, Office for National Statistics, Home Office and HMICFRS web sources only; API transport semantics, outcome-file linkage, address and postcode allocation, SAPE quality designations and corrections, PEEL cycle scope and outcome-framework interpretation; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police API authentication and response contract
verified_claims: the Police API no longer requires authentication
successful requests return HTTP 200
failed requests return a non-200 status code
limitations: HTTP 200 proves transport success rather than semantic completeness
non-200 responses must be retained by status and not converted to empty data

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Street-level outcomes query modes
verified_claims: street-level outcomes can be requested by a specific location identifier
latitude and longitude requests cover a one-mile radius
custom polygons can define a requested area
limitations: query modes are not geometrically interchangeable
one-mile and custom-area results remain based on approximate published crime locations

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Street-level outcomes date and volume limits
verified_claims: the latest available month is used when date is omitted
custom areas containing more than 10,000 outcomes return HTTP 503
the optional date parameter uses YYYY-MM
limitations: default latest month is mutable and must be pinned for reproducibility
HTTP 503 is not evidence of zero outcomes

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Street-level outcome response fields
verified_claims: outcome category contains an internal code and human-readable name
date identifies the outcome month
person_id is supplied only where available
limitations: person_id absence is not evidence that no suspect or offender exists
outcome month is not an exact event timestamp

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police outcome upload and crime linkage
verified_claims: uploaded outcome records contain an Offence Reference
outcomes are joined to the original crime using that reference
other internal court-result matching references are not published
limitations: the public dataset cannot independently reconstruct unpublished internal linkage keys
a successful public join does not prove that every court record was matched

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police outcome anonymisation fields
verified_claims: raw outcome dates are truncated to year and month before publication
outcome category is published without that date-style anonymisation
offence references are not published in CSV or API
limitations: month-only dates cannot support day-level timeliness analysis
category preservation does not remove other coverage or matching limitations

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk CSV Context field
verified_claims: Context is intended for additional human-readable force information
the documentation says newly added CSV Context fields are currently always empty
empty Context is a documented publication condition
limitations: the condition may change in future releases
empty Context must not be interpreted as evidence that no contextual information exists operationally

sources.name: National Statistics UPRN Lookup methodology
verified_claims: NSUL allocates each current Great Britain address to an Output Area using UPRN and point-in-polygon
the OA is then related to higher statistical geographies using Census-population best fit
the product is used with Ordnance Survey AddressBase
limitations: higher-geography fields can be best fit rather than direct point intersection
the product requirement and address vintage must be recorded

sources.name: ONS UPRN Directory methodology
verified_claims: ONSUD allocates addresses directly to administrative, health and other geographies
allocation uses the UPRN grid reference and point-in-polygon
ONSUD is distinct from NSUL's OA then best-fit route
limitations: NSUL and ONSUD fields must not be mixed without method metadata
address-level allocation does not validate the internal parcel-point source used by this slot

sources.name: NSUL and ONSUD product availability
verified_claims: NSUL and ONSUD cover Great Britain
both are released every six weeks
both are supplied as CSV with accompanying user guides
limitations: a six-week cadence means latest files are mutable over time
release edition and content hash are required for reproducibility

sources.name: ONS postcode product methods
verified_claims: NSPL allocates postcodes to OAs and then higher geographies using Census-population best fit
ONSPD links postcodes directly to administrative, health and other areas using point-in-polygon
ONS states the higher-geography methods differ
limitations: the two products can legitimately assign different higher-geography relationships
product name and edition must be retained with every lookup result

sources.name: ONS Postcode Directory scope
verified_claims: ONSPD covers current and terminated UK postcodes
it links postcodes to geographic areas using point-in-polygon
the product incorporates Gridlink consortium data
limitations: terminated-postcode records require valid date semantics
postcode assignment is not equivalent to an address or parcel point

sources.name: Postcode boundary-straddle allocation
verified_claims: a postcode containing addresses on both sides of a boundary is assigned using the mean grid reference of its addresses
the whole postcode can therefore be allocated to one area
some addresses may lie in the other area
limitations: postcode assignment can misallocate individual addresses near boundaries
it must not replace exact parcel point-in-polygon evidence

sources.name: Postal geography change limitations
verified_claims: postcode boundaries are subject to continuous change
postcodes can be recoded
a postcode can be reused in a different place after two years
limitations: postcode-only historical joins require effective dates
continuous monitoring is required to avoid geographic misallocation

sources.name: ONS postcode release cadence and resolution
verified_claims: ONS postcode products are released quarterly
scheduled months are February, May, August and November
products include grid references at one-metre resolution
limitations: one-metre coordinate resolution does not make a postcode an exact address boundary
quarterly edition must be pinned

sources.name: SAPE QMI output designation
verified_claims: SAPE outputs include accredited official statistics, official statistics in development and supporting information
designation depends on geography and age disaggregation
one status cannot be assigned to the entire workbook
limitations: designation must be attached at field and geography granularity
supporting information is not automatically accredited

sources.name: SAPE collection and frequency contract
verified_claims: SAPE frequency is annual
the estimates are compiled from third-party data
geographic coverage is England and Wales
limitations: annual population estimates are not monthly exposure denominators
third-party administrative inputs retain their own quality limitations

sources.name: SAPE role between censuses
verified_claims: SAPE are the official source of small-area population estimates between censuses
OAs and SOAs are building-block geographies
the products support construction of customised-area estimates
limitations: custom aggregation inherits lookup and best-fit limitations
official source status does not imply exact parcel population

sources.name: SAPE accredited geography-age scope
verified_claims: LSOA broad-age-by-sex estimates are accredited official statistics
MSOA five-year-age-by-sex estimates are accredited
health-geography estimates are accredited
limitations: accreditation does not extend automatically to finer LSOA age detail or OA estimates
denominator selection must match the accredited scope

sources.name: SAPE fine age-disaggregation status
verified_claims: single-year-age SOA estimates are supporting information
LSOA five-year age detail has not automatically demonstrated accredited quality
users are warned about fine age-detail limitations
limitations: fine age cells must not inherit broad-age accreditation
small-cell precision is not equivalent to accuracy

sources.name: SAPE geography-specific development status
verified_claims: electoral ward estimates are official statistics in development
Westminster constituency and National Park estimates are in development
health geographies are direct LSOA aggregations and accredited
limitations: development outputs have not demonstrated all accreditation criteria
status must not be collapsed across geographies

sources.name: SAPE faulty OA lookup correction
verified_claims: ONS identified a faulty lookup splitting 2011 OAs to 2021 OAs
many new 2021 OAs had received zero share of parent population
the correction was applied on 12 March 2025 to ONS and Nomis
limitations: pre-correction OA-derived files are unsafe without edition checks
ONS states accredited LSOA, MSOA and health outputs were not affected

sources.name: SAPE population-definition limitation
verified_claims: SAPE cover the usually resident population
they do not represent workday populations
short-term visitors are outside the estimate definition
limitations: resident denominators may not represent transient exposure to crime
tourism, commuting and event populations require separate evidence

sources.name: SAPE ratio-change limitation
verified_claims: ratio change assumes administrative-data change is a proxy for population change
the assumption works reasonably for most areas
administrative processes such as list cleaning can cause issues
limitations: administrative change is not direct observation of true population
local anomalies require quality review

sources.name: SAPE benchmark and uncertainty limitation
verified_claims: outside census comparisons there are no benchmark population counts for SAPE
migrants and students are harder to estimate
errors may grow over time in areas with larger hard-to-estimate populations
limitations: annual coherence does not remove inter-censal uncertainty
population-denominator confidence must remain separate from crime-data confidence

sources.name: SAPE statistical disclosure control
verified_claims: SAPE are subject to statistical disclosure control
selected cells receive small adjustments
the underlying Census base for some fine LSOA cells was rounded to the nearest five
limitations: published cells are not exact underlying person counts
small adjustments must not be reverse-engineered or treated as measurement error

sources.name: Census 2021 output-geography best fit
verified_claims: Census 2021 estimates for output geographies aggregate whole OAs
OAs are best-fitted to the geography current at publication
ONS states this supports consistency, comparability and non-disclosure
limitations: best-fit values are not exact boundary estimates
publication geography date must be retained

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: PEEL assessment scope
verified_claims: PEEL assesses all 43 police forces in England and Wales
the programme evaluates effectiveness, efficiency and legitimacy
force reports and grades are published
limitations: PEEL is force-level inspection evidence rather than parcel evidence
published grades do not directly measure LSOA crime incidence

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: PEEL cycle adaptation
verified_claims: PEEL questions do not remain identical for every inspection cycle
questions adapt to changing policing priorities and circumstances
cycle methodology is published separately
limitations: grades from different cycles may not measure identical constructs
cross-cycle trend analysis requires framework mapping

sources.publisher: His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services
sources.name: PEEL latest and historical report access
verified_claims: the service exposes the latest grade for each force
previous reports remain separately accessible
the 2025 to 2027 cycle has its own methodology and questions
limitations: latest does not mean contemporaneous across every force publication date
report date and cycle must be retained

sources.name: Crime Outcomes Framework purpose
verified_claims: the Outcomes Framework recognises the full range of disposals
no one outcome is intended to be favoured over others
the emphasis is appropriateness rather than hitting targets
limitations: outcome categories must not be ordinally ranked as better or worse
outcome mix is not a direct force or parcel safety score

sources.name: Crime Outcomes Framework victim-oriented rationale
verified_claims: the framework was designed to strengthen police discretion
it sought to remove incentives to pursue outcomes perceived as better
it intended to support a more victim-oriented approach
limitations: the stated policy rationale is not measured outcome effectiveness
administrative outcome categories must not be converted to welfare rankings

sources.name: Monthly crime-outcome submission exclusions
verified_claims: monthly force crime and outcome data described in the annex exclude fraud
Computer Misuse Act offences are also excluded
the exclusion also applies to the described transferred or cancelled records stream
limitations: published totals are not all-crime totals unless scope is stated
excluded offence families require separate sources

sources.name: Current HODH and Crimsec4 force coverage
verified_claims: at publication 43 forces supplied monthly crime, outcomes and transfer-cancel data solely through HODH
one remaining force supplied Crimsec4 returns
the Home Office stated an intention to move that force to HODH
limitations: source-system coverage is a publication-date snapshot
record-level and aggregate source capabilities remain different during transition
